subject: Scope & Data Flow Clarifications for HelixOps Integration — MSA/DPA Redlines
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@helixops.io>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@helixops.io, dan.oconnor@helixops.io
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HelixOps -> Redwood: initial DPA + questions on data flows

Hi Rachel / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — HelixOps is excited about the connector. I've attached a marked-up DPA with our standard data residency and deletion language. A couple of asks up front so we can scope the SOW: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted connector will persist any HelixOps customer PII in long-term logs or trace stores beyond 30 days? Our security team requires a data retention cap.
- The integration will route platform telemetry to Redwood for model selection. Will any telemetry be used for training or model improvement?
- We flagged the subprocessor list (Appendix B) — please confirm if any new subs will be added for the Dedicated/Private options.

Attached: HelixOps_DPA_redline_20261122.pdf (redlines).

Can we target an internal review by Tuesday 11/24? If possible, please copy in Karthik on procurement.

Best,
Maya Patel
Head of Platforms | HelixOps
maya@helixops.io

--
Attachment: HelixOps_DPA_redline_20261122.pdf (PDF, 42 pages — redline comments embedded)

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@helixops.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixOps -> Redwood: initial DPA + questions on data flows

Maya — thanks for the redlines and clear questions. Looping in Vanessa (legal) and Sergio (solutions/engineering) to get precise answers. High level responses below: 

- Retention: Hosted API retains request/response logs for 30 days by default; we can contractually cap retention to 30 days for HelixOps production traffic and configure access controls.
- Training: Redwood does not use customer request/response data to train models unless a customer opts in; we can include that in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: Our current list is in Appendix B; Dedicated and Private deployments do not add subprocessors, but Dedicated may use a managed infra partner in certain regions — we will confirm exact names.

Vanessa / Sergio / Karthik — could you review the attached redline and provide proposed language changes for the DPA and a short note for the MSA carveouts (data flow diagram + SOW bullets) by EOD Tue 11/24? Procurement will need an estimated SOW outline and timeline.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com

--

Thanks, Rachel / Maya. I reviewed HelixOps' redline and drafted proposed language and a short carveout summary. Main edits attached in a doc: Redwood_MSADPA_comments_20261124.docx. Highlights: 

1) Retention clause: replace open-ended "log retention" language with a contractual cap of 30 days for production request/response logs; add an exception process for forensic retention (w/ customer written approval).

2) Training & Use: insert explicit "no training without consent" clause and define "use for improvement" scope — telemetry used for product telemetry/ops anonymized aggregates only.

3) Subprocessors: commit to current Appendix B and a 30-day notice for any changes. For Dedicated in EU, we will name the managed infra partner (EdgeVault Ltd.) in Appendix B.

4) Data flow diagram: I created a simple ASCII flow in the doc and added an SOW bullet: "Redwood will provide connector dev + test environment and ensure no customer PII is present in telemetry exports; export format and fields to be agreed in SOW."

Open questions for engineering (Sergio): need a short note confirming whether any debug/trace IDs include customer-identifying tokens and whether those are retained beyond 30 days. Also need a short paragraph about our default disk encryption/keys for Dedicated.

I've marked up the DPA and added a tracked changes version — attaching.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Redwood_MSADPA_comments_20261124.docx

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Maya Patel <maya@helixops.io>, legal@helixops.io
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: HelixOps -> Redwood: initial DPA + questions on data flows

Hi all — quick engineering confirmation: 

- Debug/trace IDs: by default we include short trace IDs that are pseudorandom tokens, not customer PII. We do not log raw HelixOps credentials or token payloads.
- Telemetry retention: request/response KV and prefix cache metadata is retained up to 30 days; we can configure an enforced retention policy for HelixOps-managed traffic.
- Disk encryption: Dedicated uses AES-256 at rest with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations where requested (we've noted EdgeVault for EU Dedicated).

I'll attach a one-page ops note for the SOW describing runtime behavior and controls. Expect that in the next message.

— Sergio Alvarez
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
